svg.aria-label: Parallax global chaining: one dynamic-programming pass over every seed on every chromosome and strand, costing each move between seeds in bits, so indels, structural breaks and repeats compete on one scale.
svg.text: Global chaining: the read’s best explanation, scored in bits
One dynamic-programming pass over every seed on every chromosome and strand.
Each move between seeds costs −log2 of its probability, so indels, structural breaks and repeats compete on one scale.
each seed earns +2 bits per new read base
Schematic, not to scale. Default parameters; bits = −log2 P.
Extend the chain one seed at a time
The first case starts a chain at seed i; the second extends the best
chain ending at an earlier seed j. new(j, i) counts the read bases
i covers past the end of j, so no base is credited twice. Seeds are
sorted by read end and scanned once, across all chromosomes and strands.
An indel is costed as a break whenever that is cheaper.
The k-th distinct locus costs 40·(k − 1) bits; a locus is the seeds
within 20 kb of each other on one chromosome. Loci are dropped one
at a time, re-running the pass, while the score improves.
Moves within one locus (≤ 5 kb) stay in one record and their gaps
are aligned; any other move starts a supplementary record.
